destination.name: Hangzhou
destination.tagline: A lakeside city of temples, pagodas, tea hills and canal-side old streets
destination.description: Hangzhou is built around West Lake, a UNESCO World Heritage freshwater lake ringed by hills, causeways, islands and pagodas. Beyond the shoreline, Lingyin Temple and its rock-carved Buddhas sit in the western hills, Dragon Well tea is grown in Longjing's terraces, and Xixi Wetland Park threads waterways through the city's west. The old Qinghefang quarter, the Grand Canal and the Qiantang River add street food, history and a river-side pagoda, and the walled city of Liangzhu is 5,300 years old.
whyVisit: Stroll the causeways of West Lake

goodToKnow.title: Plan the west hills apart
goodToKnow.detail: Lingyin Temple, the Longjing tea hills and Xixi Wetland lie west of West Lake, so give them their own half-days.

goodToKnow.title: Walk the lake causeways
goodToKnow.detail: Su Causeway, built in 1089, crosses West Lake on six bridges, and Yanggong Causeway runs past Guo's Villa.

goodToKnow.title: Arrive by high-speed rail
goodToKnow.detail: The Shanghai to Hangzhou high-speed line serves the city, so a train is the simplest way to arrive from Shanghai.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Spring blossom and clear autumn days: {months}. Summers are hot, June is rainy.
